name: Hotjar
label: Hotjar — survey REST v1 + survey webhook ingress
description: Official Hotjar HTTP API v1 at https://api.hotjar.io. Handler: OfficialApiNode. OAuth client-credentials is fetched by the operator; paste the access token as Bearer (this node does not call /v1/oauth/token). Survey list/get/responses and user lookup. Supports survey_response and recording metadata webhooks. Identify/Events are browser JavaScript only and are not operations. No heatmap export and no recording scrape. Customer owns the Hotjar site. Survey answers are PII. Never log access_token. Inbound webhooks: selecting the :listen operation (trigger.listen) via webhook_key ($webhookKeyRef) blocks the canvas INPUT port and compiles as a webhook-triggered Message Start (or binds to any Activity's MESSAGE Boundary Event).
author: 5c8b0d45-1d10-4f2e-844c-2318af96b2fa

ports.name: input
ports.description: site_id (or config), survey_id, pagination, user_id. trigger.listen does not call HTTP — paste the StudioQuack ingress URL in Hotjar webhook UI. Do not put access_token here. Example: {"operation":"survey.response.list","survey_id":"survey_…","limit":"100"}.

schema.label: operation
schema.description: Overrides config. EXACT: 'survey.list' | 'survey.get' | 'survey.response.list' | 'user.lookup' | 'trigger.listen'. trigger.listen (:listen role) is configured on the node via webhook_key ($webhookKeyRef) for inbound webhooks (blocks the canvas INPUT port).

schema.label: site_id
schema.description: Hotjar site id (Sites & Organizations). Path param; config is used when input is blank.

schema.label: survey_id
schema.description: Survey id for get and response.list. e.g. survey_…

schema.label: organization_id
schema.description: Hotjar organization id for user.lookup (path {organization_id}, required); shown next to the organization on the Sites & Organizations page. Example: 123456.

schema.label: data_subject_email
schema.description: Email of the data subject for user.lookup (GDPR access/erasure). Send this and/or data_subject_site_id_to_user_id_map. Hotjar emails the report to this address unless delete_all_hits is true. Example: jane@example.com.

schema.label: data_subject_site_id_to_user_id_map
schema.description: Map of Hotjar site id to your own user id (as sent via the Identify API) for user.lookup; alternative or complement to data_subject_email. Example: {"42":"unique_id_42"}.

schema.label: delete_all_hits
schema.description: user.lookup: true silently and irreversibly deletes all data found for the subject (no report email); false (default) only produces a data report. Example: false.

ports.name: output
ports.description: Success: status=ok, http_status, data (surveys/responses). Inbound webhook events (:listen) emit normalized event data on output. Errors raise a BPMN error for the error boundary event (INVALID_INPUT, AUTH_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED, HTTP_<status>, REQUEST_FAILED); secrets are redacted.

configurationParameters.label: Operation
configurationParameters.description: Default operation when input.operation is blank. Selecting trigger.listen (:listen role) reveals webhook_key ($webhookKeyRef), blocks the canvas INPUT port, and compiles as a webhook-triggered Message Start or Activity MESSAGE Boundary Event.

configurationParameters.label: Access token
configurationParameters.description: Pre-fetched OAuth access token from POST https://api.hotjar.io/v1/oauth/token (grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret). Sent as Authorization: Bearer. Tokens expire (~3600s). Keys expire after 1 year. Never log. Ask Scale / Observe Scale plan-gated.

configurationParameters.label: Site ID
configurationParameters.description: Default Hotjar site id used as path {site_id} when input.site_id is blank.

configurationParameters.label: Webhook Key
configurationParameters.description: Engine Webhook API Key binding ($webhookKeyRef) routing inbound HTTP webhooks to this node.
